findings.title: Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy and rejections are unhandled
findings.body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module-evaluation time. Dynamic `import()` starts loading as soon as the expression is evaluated, so every app module is still fetched and evaluated the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported — the PR's stated goal (async/lazy loading of app packages) is not achieved, and bundlers still have to include every app in the graph. Worse, the 28 promises are created with no attached handlers at module scope: if any app module throws while being evaluated (bad env/config, side-effectful module), the resulting rejection is unhandled and can crash the Node process (unhandled rejections are fatal by default on modern Node) even when that app is never used. To get real laziness and safe error handling the values should be thunks/getters, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`.

findings.title: Commented example import points to a non-existent path
findings.body: The placeholder comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example"` to `// example: import("./example")`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so anyone uncommenting this line (its only purpose) gets a module-not-found error. The comment should read `example: import("./_example")`.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions use an async forEach and are never awaited
findings.body: In the recurring branch the code does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises, so the callbacks only run after the synchronous part of `handler` finishes; `apiDeletes` is still empty when `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs at line 652 and when the 200 response is returned. The external calendar events for all remaining recurring instances are therefore deleted fire-and-forget (and any failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of being reported). Now that `getCalendar` is async this gap is larger than before. The same block in the `else` branch was correctly converted to a `for ... of` loop in this PR; this branch should use `for ... of` (or `await Promise.all(map(...))`) too.

findings.title: requestReschedule: async callback in forEach means cancellations are not awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now asynchronous, the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email, fire webhooks and return while the calendar/video event deletions are still pending, and any error (e.g. expired credentials) becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` so failures are observable and the work completes before the request ends.

findings.title: try/catch no longer protects the now-async forEach callback
findings.body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async`, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can never catch anything thrown inside it: rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` escape as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged, and `Reschedule` returns `true` and sends the reschedule email before the calendar/video events are actually cancelled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: try/catch no longer protects the now-async forEach callback
findings.body: Same problem as in the vital app: making the `forEach` callback `async` means the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from `await getCalendar(...)`, `calendar.deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`; they become unhandled promise rejections, and the function returns `true` / sends the reschedule email before the external events are cancelled. Await the work explicitly, e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns pending promises in its `calendar` field
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous but `getCalendar(credential)` now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`, so each returned item's `calendar` property is a promise rather than a `Calendar`. This silently changes the public shape of `ReturnType<typeof getCalendarCredentials>` for every consumer (only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated here); any other caller that uses `item.calendar` directly will get a promise object at runtime. Additionally the promises are created without handlers, so if a CalendarService constructor/import rejects for a credential that is never awaited, the rejection goes unhandled. Consider making the function `async` and resolving the calendars (e.g. with `Promise.all`) before returning, so the contract stays `Calendar | null`.
